title: Talent or Luck? Evaluating Attribution Bias in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Using male and female name proxies in prompts to measure differences in how models attribute success and failure to internal factors (effort, ability) versus external factors (luck, task difficulty) across multiple societal scenarios.

Evaluating attribution asymmetries by substituting name proxies from 15 different nationalities and calculating the internal-external differential for event outcomes in single-actor, actor-actor, and actor-observer settings.
Measuring the internal-external attribution differential for success and failure using name proxies representing six racial groups to compare the assignment of internal versus external causes.
Assessing attribution gaps by using name proxies associated with six major religions to observe whether models disproportionately credit or blame specific religious identities for outcomes.
